On Tue, Aug 3, 2027 at 09:12 AM Asha Patel <asha@skyline.ai> wrote:
> We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and 5xx errors across our inference endpoints since ~08:50 UTC.

Team — quick findings from the production telemetry and KV ring traces:
- Root pattern looks like cache thrash induced by large numbers of cold prefixes mixed with aggressive prefix sharing. Many short requests are causing frequent KV invalidations and cache churn.
- The KV ring shows sustained queue buildup on lanes 3 and 4 (hot partition), causing HOL (head-of-line) blocking in batch lanes. When lane build-up hits the backpressure threshold, the runtime sheds requests with 502/504 gateway errors.
- Continuous batching increased effective batch age for small requests; under hot partitions this amplifies latency variance.

Immediate actions taken (12:05–12:18 UTC):
1) Temporarily disabled continuous batching on Skyline routes (runtime flag: runtime.batch.continuous=false). Latency improved slightly but still above SLO due to KV contention.
2) Applied a temporary KV write-throttle (kv.ring.write_qps=1200 -> 600) to reduce thrash; this cut error-rate but reduced throughput.
3) Provisioned 2 extra KV shards for Skyline's tenant ring to reduce per-shard hotness (requires rolling restart of shard owners).

Recommended next steps (to finish stabilization):
- Approve a rolling restart of 6 inference nodes to pick up kv-config-before.after.patch (this will apply the conservative TTL and disable prefix-sharing). Expected disruption: brief (~20–40s) warmup for restarted nodes; we will drain and roll.
- Post-mitigation: run longer-term fixes — KV hotspot redistribution, adaptive shard assignment, and an improved prefix-eviction policy.

I've attached kv-metrics-20270803.png and kv-config-before.after.patch that contain the diff I want applied. If approved I can schedule the rolling restart at 13:00 UTC.

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

3) Follow-up in 48h with a postmortem and longer-term roadmap: KV redistribution, adaptive eviction, and improved batching heuristics.
